races.name: EMS Copiers Irish EBF Fillies Maiden

runners_data.name: Arizonaneargalway
runners_data.comment: Sired by Arizona and bought for just 5,000 euros, this filly rates a modest 46 on debut, our outsider here. A dam who was useful over a mile and a half-sister who shone at six furlongs offer encouragement, but she still has plenty to find against this field.

runners_data.name: Concorde Landed
runners_data.comment: A notable 200,000-euro breeze-up purchase by Sioux Nation, she's out of a dam who excelled over five and six furlongs as a juvenile, with a half-sister useful at a mile, and rates second-highest here at 75. She may just need this experience before showing her best.

runners_data.name: Fly Smartly
runners_data.comment: A costly 135,000-euro daughter of Mehmas, out of a dam smart over seven furlongs at two, rates a strong 73 with us. The yard is out of sorts lately (just one success from 20 runners), so she's perhaps one to note rather than side with on debut.

runners_data.name: My Irish Lady
runners_data.comment: A 160,000-euro filly by Minzaal whose unraced dam is a half-sister to a Graded-placed performer in the US, she's only our second-lowest rated runner here at 62 on debut. The yard is firing on all cylinders currently, which offers her the best chance of outrunning that figure.

runners_data.name: Shi Yang
runners_data.comment: Fifth on her only start, beaten four lengths in a maiden here, this filly races back over the same course, distance and good going just ten days later and rates 74 with us, third best in this field. A wide stall is the obvious concern, but there should be more to come.

runners_data.name: Snowing
runners_data.comment: Beaten nine lengths on her Curragh debut, this filly steps out for a trainer with a strong record at today's track and rates 81 with us, the highest in this field, over suitable trip and ground. A six-week break is the only slight worry.

runners_data.name: Southern Boulevard
runners_data.comment: A 110,000-euro daughter of No Nay Never, out of a dam smart over six furlongs at two and with a half-sister who shone at a mile, rates 73 with us. The stable landed this race last year and clearly respects her chance on debut.

runners_data.name: Woodlawn Lily
runners_data.comment: Sixth then fourth in two starts, including when well held stepped up in grade at this course last time, this speedily-bred filly rates 68 with us. A short break and a yard in good form both work in her favour, but she needs to leave those below-par efforts behind her.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Race

runners_data.name: Howd'yadoit
runners_data.note: G M Lyons in sharp form (8/17 past fortnight) and Gary Carroll booked for this 3yo who recorded a recent course win over 5f on Good; naturally prominent and expected to track Keke in a perfect stalking position throughout.
runners_data.comment: Fairyhouse last time was a stay-related flop over six furlongs, but this gelding won going away before that and drops back to the minimum trip today over conditions that suit. Rated 99 with us, fourth in this quintet, he can bounce back for a trainer in form.

runners_data.name: Keke
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a strong 12-from-15 record on Good ground and a course win at 6f; faces no pressure from rivals today so can dictate fractions entirely on her own terms, which is where she is most dangerous at OR 102.
runners_data.comment: A consistent sort who ran creditably in defeat in a Listed race at Cork last time, this gelding wears a tongue-tie for the first time and rates the pick of this quintet at 101. A strongly run five furlongs on a sound surface should suit down to the ground.

runners_data.name: Likedbymike
runners_data.note: Last ran just six days ago and returned two places in most recent starts over this exact trip on similar ground, suggesting consistent competitiveness; a natural hold-up horse who will need either a fast pace or a gap to appear, both of which are uncertain in a five-runner field with one front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Below her best when never a threat from off the pace at the Curragh last time, this filly still rates second-highest in this quintet at 100 with us, and her share of places shows she's competitive at this level. A modest strike-rate is the concern, but she's respected on figures.

runners_data.name: Cardiff By The Sea
runners_data.note: Sole career win came on Soft ground and the two Good-ground runs in recent history read 7th and 4th, raising a mild but genuine concern about whether she tops out on a quicker surface; positioned at the rear naturally and needs this pace shape to be kinder than it likely will be.
runners_data.comment: A genuine speedster who performed up to expectation when beaten four lengths in a Listed race at Ayr last time, this filly rates 99 with us, third of this quintet, and looks sure to relish a sharply run five furlongs. Faster ground would be the ideal conditions for her.

runners_data.name: Xerling
runners_data.note: Won on Good over 5f and placed again next time at the same trip, showing genuine aptitude for these conditions — however, this horse's true style is a hold-up runner pushed into a midfield map position because the field carries more closers than can all get to the rear; the style displacement tempers confidence in this scenario playing to its strengths.
runners_data.comment: This filly won readily by a length and a half in a Cork maiden last time but faces a stiff step up in company here, rating only 85 with us, bottom of this quintet. Versatile on ground and effective at both five and six furlongs, she's up against much higher-rated rivals today.

races.paceDynamic: Keke is the only confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival to press or challenge her early, meaning she is expected to set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on Good turf over five furlongs at Naas. Howd'yadoit will track closely in a prominent position just behind Keke, likely travelling in second or third, creating a straightforward two-length lead scenario into the straight with no scramble for early position. The hold-up trio of Likedbymike, Cardiff By The Sea, and Xerling will be settled in behind, though with three horses naturally wanting cover in a small field, some will inevitably be closer to the pace than their handlers might ideally prefer. This shape — a single, unhurried pace-setter dictating terms — strongly favours prominent racers who can land a few lengths off a controlled fractions and pounce in the final furlong, rather than pure closers who need a fast-run race to generate the momentum to reel in the leader; Keke herself, if allowed to coast uncontested, is equally well served.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Keke controls, front wins
scenarios.trigger: If Keke bowls along uncontested and maintains a comfortable tempo that never truly stretches those tracking her.
scenarios.body: If Keke bowls along uncontested and maintains a comfortable tempo that never truly stretches those tracking her.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker pounces late
scenarios.trigger: If Howd'yadoit travels smoothly in Keke's slipstream and Gary Carroll delivers a well-timed challenge from the two-furlong marker.
scenarios.body: If Howd'yadoit travels smoothly in Keke's slipstream and Gary Carroll delivers a well-timed challenge from the two-furlong marker.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse finishes fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely sedate enough to compress the field and one of the hold-up horses produces a sharp late burst to score.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely sedate enough to compress the field and one of the hold-up horses produces a sharp late burst to score.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses, closers swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Keke is taken on early or the early fractions prove quicker than expected, setting up a sprint finish that favours the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: If Keke is taken on early or the early fractions prove quicker than expected, setting up a sprint finish that favours the hold-up horses.

watchPoints.text: Watch Keke's early sectionals — if she is gifted a completely uncontested lead, the small field and controlled pace could see her simply coast home without being asked a serious question.
Cardiff By The Sea's record on Good ground is markedly inferior to her Soft-ground form; if the surface is riding on the firmer side of Good, discount her chances significantly in running.
With three hold-up horses in a five-runner field, Likedbymike and Xerling in particular may find themselves closer to the pace than intended, effectively racing out of their most effective position.

Howd'yadoit's jockey Gary Carroll will likely dictate the race's shape from second position — watch how close Carroll elects to sit to Keke turning in, as a tight quarter-length gap could make the difference between winning and chasing.

races.name: Coolmore Stud Blackbeard Tipperary Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Abletai
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs pace to close into; Grassick yard has been quiet (0/0 T14), 56 days since last run, but sim-going record of 2/2 placings on Good is encouraging — will need the race to develop strongly to get competitive from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: A close second, beaten only a head in a maiden at this course last time, this colt showed clear progress from debut and rates 87 with us, mid-field of ten. He needs more again stepping up in grade, and has had a lengthy break, but conditions should suit.

runners_data.name: Carry The Flag
runners_data.note: High-volume A.P. O'Brien runner with Ronan Whelan and a solid Good-ground 5f win on the book; last seen 14 days ago and in excellent recent form (2-1-2-9), making him the most credible prominent challenger to Big Negotiator if he secures a clean second-off slot.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a Group 2 at Ascot last time over the minimum trip, this colt seemed to want further that day. His overall form, including a recent win, still marks him out as the one to beat here, rating top of this field at 101, with his trainer excelling at this course.

runners_data.name: Hanney Boy
runners_data.note: Three-run 2yo with three consecutive places including a third on Good at Naas; wants a prominent position but with four horses seeking those berths he is vulnerable to being squeezed back, which would significantly diminish his chance on a flat 5f with measured gallop.
runners_data.comment: Third, beaten a length and a quarter, when dropped to five furlongs on good ground at Navan last time, this colt looks capable of more but may need it stepping up in company. He rates 84 with us and is versatile at both five and six furlongs on soft or good.

runners_data.name: Rejoinder
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and entirely unknown (no recorded form string, no LR days), trained by Robson De Aguiar alongside stablemate Belle Island; running style unclassified — a genuine unknown quantity whose chance cannot be assessed from available data.
runners_data.comment: An 82,000-euro breeze-up purchase by Space Blues and half-brother to the high-class Thunder Beauty, a mile performer, this colt rates a bold 89 with us on debut, third in this field of ten. It's admittedly a stiff task first time out, but the pedigree package points to a leading threat.

runners_data.name: Arrowstock
runners_data.note: Sole run produced a sixth of eleven on Good at Naas over 5f — uninspiring on face value but lightly raced and unclassified; Nathan Crosse riding for Daniel McLoughlin, who has had limited recent action (1/9 T14), making this a speculative entry with upside dependent on unseen ability.
runners_data.comment: Beaten eight lengths on debut in a maiden at Navan, this filly has speed in her pedigree and should take a step forward for that initial experience, but she rates bottom of this ten-strong field at 74 with us. She looks to have plenty to find against these rivals.

runners_data.name: Belle Island
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle is a major positive in the saddle; the filly has placed twice from three starts but those came on Standard/Standard-to-Slow, and Good ground at Naas is untested for her — a hold-up horse who needs things to fall perfectly on a flat 5f.
runners_data.comment: Sent forward too soon and outclassed when comfortably held in a 2yo race at the Curragh last time, this filly needs to recover that form and rates 84 with us, mid-pack in this field of ten. Speedily bred and suited by sound ground, she has been fairly fresh off an eleven-week break.

runners_data.name: Big Negotiator
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, with a Good-ground 5f win at Naas already on his record and a tongue-tie fitted; W.J. Lee for Paul Twomey, 17 days since last run, recent form shows a sharp improvement — he controls the gallop and his fate.
runners_data.comment: Below her best when beaten seven lengths in the Group 2 Queen Mary at Ascot last time, this filly - fitted with cheekpieces today - had been progressive before that, including a win, and rates 94 with us, second of this ten. She's effective over five and six furlongs on quicker ground, though that Ascot run did expose some limitations up in grade.

runners_data.name: Brazilian Diva
runners_data.note: Won on Good over 5f at Naas ten days ago and is sharp and in form; Diego Lima keeps the ride and the trainer has been active (1/5 T14) — her recent winner's confidence and suitability to these conditions make her a prominent runner to respect in the scramble for early position.
runners_data.comment: Getting off the mark readily by two and a quarter lengths in a maiden at this course last time, this filly steps up in grade today and rates 89 with us, fourth of this ten. She's effective at both five and six furlongs on a sound surface, though there's plenty more required to confirm that improvement at this level.

runners_data.name: Celestial Crown
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's runner with Ben Coen aboard; placed on soft over 5f and ran seventh on Good, so Good-ground form is unproven — lightly raced with unclassified style, yet the combination of yard and jockey keeps her relevant if she brings improvement.
runners_data.comment: Beaten ten lengths and never landing a blow from off the pace in a maiden at this course last time, this filly rates 80 with us, ninth of this ten-strong field. Effective over five furlongs on soft ground for a trainer in good form, she's difficult to recommend on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Matriarchal
runners_data.note: Has won on Good at Naas over 5f and slots into a prominent role; Rory Cleary for Josh Halley (1/7 T14) and 35 days since last run — the sim-going record (2/4 on Good, one win) gives confidence she handles the conditions, but she must navigate the positional battle early.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a novice at Lingfield last time, a below-par effort from this filly who'd won and been placed in the runs before that, she rates 83 with us, well down this field of ten. Effective at five furlongs on soft or all-weather, she faces a stiff task back up in company.

races.paceDynamic: Big Negotiator is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with W.J. Lee aboard for Paul Twomey, is likely to be sent straight to the lead from stall and allowed to bowl along at a sustainable gallop on Good ground — there is no obvious horse to push him past his comfort zone early. Carry The Flag, Brazilian Diva, Hanney Boy, and Matriarchal all want prominent positions, creating a genuine four-way scramble for the two berths directly behind Big Negotiator in the opening furlong; Carry The Flag (Ronan Whelan, high-volume A.P. O'Brien operation) and Brazilian Diva (recent Naas winner, good ground record) are likeliest to secure those slots, with Hanney Boy and Matriarchal at risk of being shuffled back slightly. The lightly-raced trio Rejoinder, Arrowstock, and Celestial Crown add positional uncertainty, while Abletai and Belle Island are the genuine hold-up runners who will be last to show. With the gallop measured rather than scorching, the race strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and sustain their effort to the line — hold-up horses face a stiff ask on a flat 5f with no true pace injection to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Big Negotiator sets a honest but uncontested gallop and the prominent horses settle just off him, the race becomes a sustained-speed test from the 2f pole.
scenarios.body: If Big Negotiator sets a honest but uncontested gallop and the prominent horses settle just off him, the race becomes a sustained-speed test from the 2f pole.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Scores Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Big Negotiator is allowed a soft lead and the prominent scrimmage behind him causes interference that allows him to steal a decisive break at halfway.
scenarios.body: If Big Negotiator is allowed a soft lead and the prominent scrimmage behind him causes interference that allows him to steal a decisive break at halfway.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent battle is fierce enough to set a genuinely strong pace and the field strings out, leaving a gap for the closers to pick through.
scenarios.body: If the prominent battle is fierce enough to set a genuinely strong pace and the field strings out, leaving a gap for the closers to pick through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly-Raced Type Bolt
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unraced or once-raced unexposed runners — Rejoinder, Arrowstock, or Celestial Crown — brings an unseen level of ability to a race where established form is modest.
scenarios.body: If one of the unraced or once-raced unexposed runners — Rejoinder, Arrowstock, or Celestial Crown — brings an unseen level of ability to a race where established form is modest.

watchPoints.text: Carry The Flag, Brazilian Diva, Hanney Boy, and Matriarchal will collide for the two slots directly behind Big Negotiator in the opening furlong — watch for bumping and checking between the 1f and 2f marks that could compromise one or more of this group.

Big Negotiator wears a tongue-tie and goes fresh (17 days); if W.J. Lee sends him sharply to the front and the prominent horses are briefly occupied fighting each other, he could steal an uncontested lead that proves very hard to reel in over flat 5f.

Rejoinder has no recorded form and an unclassified running style — watch the betting market in the final 30 minutes for any significant move that might signal the yard's private opinion of its unexposed ability.

Belle Island is 76 days since her last run and Dylan Browne McMonagle will need a strong pace to close into; if the gallop is measured, watch whether she gets any daylight at all in the final furlong rather than being held up behind a wall of horses.

Celestial Crown and Arrowstock are both lightly raced with unclassified styles — if either is strongly supported before the off, it signals that a yard with inside knowledge believes the published form underrates them significantly in a field where the ceiling of the rated horses is not dramatically high.

races.name: Lawlor's Of Naas Supporting Naas GAA Senior Football Race Day Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Arctic Steps
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 5f Good trip in recent form (1/5f/GOO) and has strong sim-going record (2W3P); a natural hold-up runner who should get a genuine closing position without redistribution, making it one of the most credibly placed late challengers in this field.
runners_data.comment: Stepped up in grade and below form when beaten eight lengths off a 74 rating last time, this filly races 2lb lower today and wears cheekpieces for the first time. Admittedly inconsistent, she rates 81 with us, third of this large field, and has previously won from the front over this trip on good or all-weather ground.

runners_data.name: Harry's Hill
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran who has been running consistently on Good ground over 5f but has not won since his sim-going W; ran just six days ago which may blunt his sharpness, and his progressive slide down the weights suggests his current form cycle is one of attrition rather than improvement.
runners_data.comment: Form has faded across a run of six of late, though this gelding performed up to that level when beaten five lengths in a handicap at the Curragh last time. He wears a tongue-tie for the first time today, rates 73 with us, mid-field of thirteen, and is best served by yielding or good ground over this trip.

runners_data.name: Lethimfly
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's four-year-old has a placed run at 3/5f/GOO in the recent string and handles this trip and going combination competently; ran 27 days ago and holds scope for improvement, and the blinkers are worth noting as a headgear flag on a horse that has shown enough raw ability to be competitive off this mark.
runners_data.comment: Race fitness issues have hampered this gelding, though he carries a fair mark on his best form and lines up from stall thirteen wearing blinkers for the first time. He went too freely too soon at a stamina-sapping track last time, well beaten in a handicap at Navan, but rates 74 with us in this field of thirteen and is suited by five furlongs on good ground.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Cry
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and the key pace-setter for this race; has won over 5f on Standard and shown ability on Good, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.94) flags that this position is not wholly natural, and any pressure from the stalls would compromise the plan — if allowed to bowl along uncontested, the stamina hold-up becomes critical at the 5f minimum.
runners_data.comment: Below form when eased off having missed the money in a handicap at Fairyhouse last time, this gelding nonetheless carries a good mark on his all-weather form and had won not long before that. He rates 83 with us, second of this large field, and is effective at five and six furlongs on going from good to yielding.

runners_data.name: White Smoke
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who has placed at 4/5f/GOO and 4/6f/STA in recent form; the 56-day absence is a concern for fitness sharpness, and she has shown a tendency to drift trip from 5f to 6f which makes the minimum distance a slight query, though Good ground suits her profile.
runners_data.comment: Down the field in a handicap at this course last time, this filly looks up against a stiff mark and rates bottom of this field at 64 with us. Fitted today with both a tongue-tie and blinkers for the first time and drawn wide, she's been inconsistent and has plenty to prove, though she is effective over six furlongs on soft or good ground.

runners_data.name: Bold Optimist
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse in character, wearing a hood; the 106-day layoff is the single biggest flag in the field, and while his recent form over 5f on Standard shows placed efforts, the fitness question on a long absence makes the STYLE_FIT discount (0.92) a secondary concern behind his racecourse readiness.
runners_data.comment: Performed to expectation when beaten three and a half lengths off a 3lb higher mark at Dundalk last time, this gelding returns from a lengthy break wearing cheekpieces for the first time from a wide draw. He rates 73 with us, mid-field of thirteen, and can defy the layoff to go well again on a sound surface over this trip.

runners_data.name: Nouvel Espoir
runners_data.note: Won at 1/5f/SOF and has placed three times over 5f on Good, giving him the best raw Good-ground form of the redistributed group; true hold-up style is crowded out by the field shape, but if traffic clears he is the redistributed runner with the most credible win form at the trip and going.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap by two lengths off a 6lb lower mark at Down Royal last time, this gelding is up in the weights again today but rates top of this large field at 84 with us. Effective at both five and six furlongs on soft or good ground, he holds obvious claims of building further on that latest success.

runners_data.name: Ardadslosttheplot
runners_data.note: David Marnane's two-year-old returning from 277 days off and stepping from 6-7f back to 5f for the first time since its juvenile campaign; the long absence, unproven stamina at the sharp minimum, and only four career runs make this one of the least predictable quantities in the race — natural closer whose true position is unlikely to materialise cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Off the track for the best part of a year, this filly was never a factor when beaten five and a half lengths in a nursery at Cork on her latest start. She rates 66 with us, well down this field of thirteen, drawn wide, and needs more to figure back after such a long layoff despite being in good form before that run.

runners_data.name: Cactus
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien's three-year-old has struggled to convert form, with a best finish of 4th over this trip, and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) reflects that the midfield map position is not its natural landing spot; on Good ground over 5f the raw ability is present but the consistent defeats suggest a horse still learning rather than one ready to win.
runners_data.comment: Down the field in a maiden at Cork last time, this filly has been somewhat below par of late but drops back into a handicap today for a trainer who excels at this course. She rates 78 with us, fourth of this large field, and is effective at both five and six furlongs on soft or good ground, though more consistency is needed.

runners_data.name: Jordan Breeze
runners_data.note: The only horse other than Sovereign Cry drawn to race prominently, with two recent 2nd-place finishes and a win over 5f on Soft; best form has come on softer ground so Good is a slight downgrade, but the prominent position in a thin-paced race makes Jordan Breeze a genuine each-way threat rather than merely a pace influence.
runners_data.comment: Faded to finish sixth, beaten six and a quarter lengths off a rating of 62 last time, a below-par effort from this gelding who has won and been runner-up twice in recent starts. Racing off the same mark today, he rates 72 with us, mid-field of thirteen, and needs to turn that form around on ground from soft to all-weather over this trip.

runners_data.name: Billboa
runners_data.note: Runs off the lowest active sim-going score of the field (1/15 on relevant going), making his form highly suspect on Good turf; the trainer has no recent winners in the T14 window and the headgear flag (t) suggests connections are searching for a solution rather than confident of one.
runners_data.comment: Stepped up in grade and well beaten in a handicap at Dundalk last time, this gelding is an unknown quantity following his time off and rates near the foot of this large field at 66 with us. He wears a tongue-tie for the first time and is best served by all-weather ground at five or six furlongs.

runners_data.name: Tawaazon
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who ran just three days ago, which is a significant freshness concern; has placed at 2/5f/GOO and 4/6f/GOO recently and handles the going, but the quick turnaround and natural hold-up profile being squeezed to midfield by field congestion means timing and recovery are both working against him here.
runners_data.comment: Quick to reappear just three days after a below-par effort in a handicap at Fairyhouse, beaten five and a quarter lengths, this gelding rates 72 with us, mid-field of thirteen, and carries a fair mark provided he rediscovers that form. He's fitted with both a tongue-tie and blinkers for the first time and is effective at five or six furlongs on soft or good ground.

runners_data.name: Phil's Dream
runners_data.note: OR=49 makes this the lowest-rated runner in the race and the weight allowance (119lbs) only partially bridges the class gap; has won at 1/5f/STA and placed at 2/5f/STA but Good going is a clear negative in the sim-going stats (2/15), and the visor and tongue-tie headgear combination speaks to a horse connections are trying to coax a performance from.
runners_data.comment: Performed up to par when beaten four and a quarter lengths in a handicap at this course last time, this gelding had been going well before that including a win, and returns fitted with a tongue-tie and visor for the first time. He rates 67 with us, near the foot of this large field, for a yard short of recent success, and needs to find extra to get his head in front off that mark.

races.paceDynamic: Sovereign Cry is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner 5f apprentice handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is set to bowl along at a sustainable, self-controlled gallop rather than face any early pressure. Jordan Breeze is the only other prominent-style runner, likely to sit just off the leader's heels and track through, meaning the early tempo is dictated by Sovereign Cry alone. The bulk of the field — Arctic Steps, Harry's Hill, Lethimfly, White Smoke, and a cluster of redistributed hold-up types including Cactus, Nouvel Espoir, Ardadslosttheplot, Bold Optimist, Billboa, Tawaazon, and Phil's Dream — are true rear-of-field runners that cannot all settle into their natural position and will crowd the midfield-to-rear bracket; the ones most likely to actually secure a genuine hold-up berth are Arctic Steps, Harry's Hill, and Lethimfly, who are legitimate stalkers with the best recent evidence of closing on Good ground. A sole pace-setter dictating an honest but unforced gallop on Good going at Naas over the minimum trip strongly favours closers and hold-up runners who can travel smoothly off that tempo and produce a sustained late run — the redistribution of so many nominal hold-up types into midfield creates a compressed, bunched chasing pack where only the most naturally fluid hold-up runners with genuine Good-ground form will navigate cleanly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sovereign Cry Controls And Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Sovereign Cry maintains a measured, front-running lead and the chasing pack's congestion prevents a clean challenge from developing.
scenarios.body: If Sovereign Cry maintains a measured, front-running lead and the chasing pack's congestion prevents a clean challenge from developing.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Runners Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the uncontested pace is just honest enough to cause Sovereign Cry to flatten out inside the final furlong, allowing genuine closers to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: If the uncontested pace is just honest enough to cause Sovereign Cry to flatten out inside the final furlong, allowing genuine closers to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fill Placings
scenarios.trigger: If Jordan Breeze tracks Sovereign Cry closely and the tempo proves too slow to reel in from the rear, leaving the front two to dominate.
scenarios.body: If Jordan Breeze tracks Sovereign Cry closely and the tempo proves too slow to reel in from the rear, leaving the front two to dominate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Midfield Horse Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If a redistributed hold-up runner — most likely Nouvel Espoir or Tawaazon — finds a clear run from the midfield mass and outruns its natural position.
scenarios.body: If a redistributed hold-up runner — most likely Nouvel Espoir or Tawaazon — finds a clear run from the midfield mass and outruns its natural position.

watchPoints.text: Sovereign Cry — monitor whether it is allowed to stride clear uncontested from the stalls; if Jordan Breeze challenges for the lead in the first furlong, the pace dynamic shifts materially and the front-runner scenario probability collapses.

Arctic Steps and Lethimfly — both are genuine hold-up runners at the back of a very compressed field of closers; watch the draw and early traffic patterns, as a poor break or blocked run will eliminate their chance before the race has properly begun.

Ardadslosttheplot — the 277-day absence combined with a drop back to 5f for the first time in this horse's career is an unpredictable wildcard; if it bounces fresh it could unsettle the pace map, but fitness on that layoff is a serious question mark.

Billboa and Phil's Dream — both are significantly disadvantaged by the Good going according to their sim-going records and are the runners most likely to be out of contention early, which may inadvertently assist the closers directly behind them by freeing up rail room in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Florida Bay
runners_data.comment: Broke his maiden by a short margin at Fairyhouse last time, also placed third before that, and with course, distance and good ground proven for a yard that landed this contest last year, rates 99 and the one to beat up in grade.

runners_data.name: One Number
runners_data.comment: Found the company too strong down the field in a Listed race at Ascot last time, though the runner-up effort before that is more encouraging form. Well suited by this going, and with room for improvement now stepping up in trip again, he's yet to win in two starts but rates a workable 86 for this test.

runners_data.name: Wo Wo Never
runners_data.comment: A big impression on debut, third but beaten 11 lengths in a maiden at Gowran Park, points to more improvement with today's trip already proven. Regarded as having real physical scope, though this looks a tougher task, and he's yet to win, rated 90.

runners_data.name: Ranting Duke
runners_data.comment: Disqualified last time, but the placed effort before that reads well — second beaten just a length in a novice at York, finishing in a manner that suggested today's step up to a mile would suit even better. A stronger sort with more still to come, but the disqualification leaves a query, and he's rated bottom of the pack on today's figures at 84.

runners_data.name: Sarah's Choice
runners_data.comment: A daughter of Blue Point out of a dam who was herself useful at 6f as a two-year-old, this 100,000-euro breeze-up purchase is a half-sister to the useful Temple Of Hera and, foaled in February, should already have the scope for this level. She steps out without any recorded form, though, and the view is that debut success may be a stretch, so respect for the pedigree should be tempered by that first-time question mark.

runners_data.name: Tosca No Candis
runners_data.comment: Showed encouraging signs on her sole start, beaten 4 lengths in an auction race at Leopardstown, with today's trip and going already proven. She's yet to win, though, and with more needed to bridge the gap in this field, she's up against it on a rating of 84.

runners_data.name: Cedrela
runners_data.comment: By Wooded and out of a family that includes a 7f winner in France, this 41,000-euro purchase — foaled in February — arrives with physical maturity and pedigree appeal, and the yard have a reputation for readying newcomers. It's a stiff race for a debutant, though, with this outing viewed more as an educational run than a serious tilt, on a rating of 93.

runners_data.name: Dancing Destiny
runners_data.comment: A below-form fourth at Fairyhouse last time, beaten 10 lengths, follows a third and a win before that, so there's more substance here than the latest line suggests. Up to a mile now, with course, distance and good ground all in her favour, she's a leading threat on 97.

runners_data.name: Drowsy Maggie
runners_data.comment: Struggled on her only start, well beaten in a maiden at Ballinrobe, with a great deal of improvement needed to figure at this level. Unproven over today's trip, and rated bottom of the field on 48, she has plenty to prove against this field.

runners_data.name: Wheres The Gold
runners_data.comment: Struggled to see out the trip when down the field in an auction race at The Curragh last time, continuing a run of four starts without a win. Conditions have yet to click for her, and although today's distance has been covered before, plenty more improvement is needed on a rating of 54.

runners_data.name: Bofa Beach
runners_data.comment: A below-form run last time, failing to last home over 10f down the field in a maiden at Gowran Park, should find today's shorter trip much more to her liking, a distance she's already proven over. A third and a fourth also feature in four starts, and with course and going both suiting, she's one of the leading dangers on 76.

runners_data.name: Donna Time
runners_data.comment: Bred with stamina in mind, she matched recent expectations when beaten 8 lengths in an auction race at Leopardstown last time, having come back from a break, with a seventh the run before. Further progress looks more likely in handicaps down the line, and she's up against it on a rating of 60 today.

runners_data.name: Mai Dahlia
runners_data.comment: Market support followed her into a maiden at Fairyhouse last time, and she rewarded that faith with a second, beaten 6 lengths, backing up a third before that. Today's mile and good ground are both proven, and with room for more up in trip plus a first-time tongue-tie added, she's a leading contender on 76.

runners_data.name: Serendipia
runners_data.comment: A well-beaten eighth here last time, some way below her true level, came after a sixth on her only other start, and there's scope for a little natural progress now that early experience is banked. A tongue-tie is added for the first time, and having had only a short break since, she's a workmanlike 60 on today's figures.

runners_data.name: Sibaza
runners_data.comment: By Night Of Thunder and out of a useful mare who excelled at 7f, this newcomer is also a half-sister to the useful Simiyann, effective over twice the trip, giving her a broad spread of inherited ability. The stable have a solid record in this race, taking it twice in the last nine runnings, and although the view is that watching her debut may be wiser than backing it, she rates the one to beat on 77.

runners_data.name: Xirivella
runners_data.comment: A Gleneagles filly who cost 23,000 euros, there's a professional pedigree and price tag behind this newcomer suggesting physical promise. The concern is that today's race looks a stiff test for a first assignment, so she may need the experience before showing her true colours, rated 64.

races.name: Care At Home Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Chapel Island
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who fades in the closing stages according to her flag, with no wins or places on good ground in similar conditions; A Oliver yard is 1/8 over 14 days and her 3yo form is modest — the step to 1m3f is untested in the win column.|
runners_data.comment: Held comfortably in a handicap at Down Royal last time, continuing a run of below-form efforts, but with course, distance and cut in the ground all proven and a first-time tongue-tie now added, there could be more to come off a mark of 60. runners_data.name: Connecteo
runners_data.note: Redistributed to the lead despite being a natural hold-up horse — Ben Coen takes the ride for A Oliver, and its only career place came over 12f on good ground, suggesting the trip suits; however, racing entirely out of role at 0.80 style fit means its chance depends heavily on a truly uncontested lead.|
runners_data.comment: Market confidence followed him into a handicap at Down Royal last time, and although beaten 8 1/2 lengths in fourth, that run has since been given a boost, with more progress expected. runners_data.name: Rodeo Blues
runners_data.note: The standout on recent form with a 1m2f good-ground win in the last 12 days for Joseph O'Brien, whose stable is firing at 10/67 in the 14-day window; DBM in the saddle is a major positive and the trip extension to 1m3f should be well within compass for this hold-up type.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap readily at Ballinrobe last time, beating that field by 3 1/4 lengths, and the belief is there's more to come. runners_data.name: The Holy Apostle
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing a hood, with a run of 14 days for Brendan Duke who is winless in four recent runners; best effort was a 5th over 7f on soft and the step to 1m3f good looks like a significant stretch.|
runners_data.comment: Struggled to see out the trip when down the field in a handicap at Down Royal last time, though he's already shown ability at 7f to a mile and should get further as he matures. runners_data.name: Captain Con
runners_data.note: Noel Meade runner returning after 29 days off, flagged as a fader who has shown nothing in recent form (7th, 6th, 10th, 13th) over varying trips on good — Adam Caffrey takes the ride and there is little evidence this 1m3f trip on a flat good track suits.|
runners_data.comment: A blend of speed and stamina in the pedigree gives hope that today's step up in trip could suit, though his recent handicap form has been well beaten, most recently at Fairyhouse. Major improvement is still needed to justify a rating of 71 against a mark of 56, but he's included among the leading dangers on our figures.

runners_data.name: Point Cartwright
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a career best of 2nd over 12f on good for Adrian McGuinness, so the trip is a potential plus; Ronan Whelan rides and the horse has placed twice at this type of distance, making it one of the more interesting hold-up candidates.|
runners_data.comment: The trip suited well when beaten just 3 1/2 lengths at Limerick last time, off a mark 2lb lower than today's, and with further scope to go up again in distance, there's more to come. Course, distance and going are all proven, and he's rated 70 on our figures, though the yard's recent form is subdued, with just one winner from 27 runners in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Maker's Mark
runners_data.note: True hold-up type pushed into midfield on the map due to the crowded rear — apprentice Sadhbh Tormey claims 7lb which softens the burden, but form is poor and the 0.91 style fit means its positional flexibility is limited.|
runners_data.comment: Raced too freely and faded late when stepped up in trip last time, comfortably held in a handicap at Down Royal, and with a sharper 7-8f seemingly more her game, today's even longer test looks a stretch further. Results have been mixed through a short career, leaving her towards the back of the pack on 55.

runners_data.name: Nephin Mountain
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse shuffled to midfield on the map; Declan McDonogh is a significant jockey booking for Michael Mulvany, and the horse has placed on good ground at 9f suggesting a stamina question at 1m3f — the redistribution discount (0.90) applies.|
runners_data.comment: Returned to form when beaten just 2 1/2 lengths off this same mark at Leopardstown last time, and with a string of fourths through his recent starts, he's a picture of consistency if unspectacular. runners_data.name: Private Larry
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on good ground which makes the trip very relevant, but recent form shows a string of poor runs (8th, 8th, 8th) and the horse is shown in midfield on the map despite being a true hold-up type; Leigh Roche rides and the 0.91 style fit is a concern in terms of positional clarity.|
runners_data.comment: A dreadful start effectively ended his chance in a handicap at Leopardstown last time, beaten 6 1/4 lengths having missed the break completely, and there should be considerably more to come from him than that. Bred for 8-10f, with today's distance already covered, and a first-time hood added, he's rated 51 against a mark of 52, low among these on official figures.

runners_data.name: Millhone
runners_data.note: Charles Weld sends out this hold-up type wearing a hood (p) — pushed into midfield due to map crowding — with a best effort of 9th on good ground at 8f and no evidence yet that 1m3f is within range; Rory Mulligan claims 5lb.|
runners_data.comment: The trip suited well when beaten 7 lengths in a handicap at Leopardstown last time, and she acts on cut ground, which should be relevant again. Further middle-distance targets look the long-term plan, and with cheekpieces fitted for the first time today, she's rated 56 against a mark of 51.

runners_data.name: Wingit

runners_data.name: Six Wings
runners_data.note: Wears headgear (tp) and is placed in midfield despite true hold-up tendencies, with all four career runs on good ground producing 7th, 6th, 9th, 13th — Paul Flynn's runner has shown no signs of winning in this sphere; Robert Whearty rides.|
runners_data.comment: Struggled to find conditions to suit in a maiden at Limerick last time, well beaten, and results have been modest throughout a short career to date. Cheekpieces are fitted for the first time today, and with today's going already proven, she's rated 66 against a mark of 50, in the middle of this large field.

runners_data.name: Darwin's Angel
runners_data.note: Jockey claim is the main angle here — Jimmy Dalton (7lb) for S M Duffy, but the horse wears a visor and returns after 57 days with a career best of 6th over 10f on good; hold-up type displaced to midfield and the style fit discount (0.90) applies.|
runners_data.comment: Out of sorts of late, well held in a claimer at Ballinrobe last time, but a first-time visor and a fresh break since could bring about a change of fortune. runners_data.name: Cadreville
runners_data.note: Best career run was a 3rd over 10f on good ground for Jarlath Fahey — the only recent near-miss in this field from a midfield hold-up position; Neve Bennett claims 7lb and if the trip extension to 1m3f is within compass this one has hidden claims.|
runners_data.comment: The trip played to his strengths when third, beaten 7 lengths, in a handicap at Gowran Park last time. There's a speedy pedigree behind him best suited to 6f, though he still needs more to make an impact in handicap company, and he's rated low in the weights on 52 against a mark of 42.

runners_data.name: Canon Law
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a fading tendency, running for Brendan Duke again — 0.93 style fit is the highest redistribution discount in the field, suggesting it is most likely to be out of position; apprentice Robyn Donaghue-Leahy rides and recent form reads 12th, 5th, 12th, 21st.|
runners_data.comment: A workmanlike sixth, 6 1/4 lengths back, in a handicap at Ballinrobe last time, and he's rated better over a shorter 7f, which is a query at today's longer trip. runners_data.name: Jewels Legacy
runners_data.note: Wears blinkers (b) and has never placed in four runs on good ground, with a best of 6th over 8f on soft — the 1m3f trip is a big step up and the 0.92 style fit means this hold-up type is unlikely to get the late run it needs from midfield.|
runners_data.comment: Struggled to last home when beaten 8 lengths in a handicap at Leopardstown last time, and she's yet to show much of note through her career so far. First-time blinkers are added today, and with 7f her more effective trip, she's towards the foot of the field on a rating of 52 against a mark of 41.

runners_data.name: Swift Charm
runners_data.note: Two thirds in a row over 10f on good ground (3rd, 3rd most recent) give this horse the most consistent recent finishing form in the race — Gavin Ryan rides for W R Crawford and the hood-and-tongue combination (ht) suggests connections are actively managing it; the trip looks ideal.|
runners_data.comment: Well held in a handicap at Down Royal last time, though a pair of thirds beforehand points to a better level, and there's a squeeze into contention if she can build on that last experience. runners_data.name: Flagstone Lady

runners_data.name: Music And Song
runners_data.note: Wore a hood (p) and ran 4th over 10f on good most recently for Thomas Dowling — natural hold-up type displaced to midfield on the map, with the redistribution discount (0.93) the joint-highest in the field; no declared jockey and the 2-of-6 good-ground record shows stamina for the trip.|
runners_data.comment: Pulled hard and could only manage fourth, beaten 10 lengths, in a claimer at Ballinrobe last time, and she's yet to show any real ability through her recent starts so far. First-time cheekpieces are added in an attempt to settle her better, and on a rating of 54 against a mark of 40, she's rated at the bottom of this field.

races.paceDynamic: Connecteo is the sole confirmed front runner in this 19-runner 1m3f handicap and has been redistributed to the lead, though its natural style is hold-up, meaning the pace it sets is unlikely to be pressured or truly genuine — expect a moderate, controlled gallop through the early and middle stages on good ground at Naas. With Connecteo effectively dictating without a natural rival for the lead, the race will be run at a sustainable tempo that compresses the field into a bunch through the back straight, setting up a severe test of late acceleration over the final two furlongs. This shape overwhelmingly favours the truest hold-up horses who can produce a sustained late run, provided they are not trapped wide or too far back in a large field — runners with confirmed closing ability and good-ground form are best positioned. The field is saturated with hold-up types: virtually every runner has been redistributed away from their natural position, meaning Connecteo, Rodeo Blues, The Holy Apostle, and Chapel Island are the horses most likely to actually secure a prominent or useful early position given their connections and jockey profiles, while the mass of redistrubuted midfield horses face a severe positional squeeze.

scenarios.body: If one of the repositioned horses — Flagstone Lady, Private Larry, or Nephin Mountain — secures a better early position than their redistribution suggests and strikes from just off the pace.

watchPoints.text: Rodeo Blues is the one to watch: a confirmed good-ground winner over 10f just 12 days ago with Dylan Browne McMonagle aboard for the in-form O'Brien yard — the step to 1m3f on identical going looks like a logical progression and this is the horse most likely to deliver a sustained finish.

Swift Charm has recorded back-to-back 3rds over the same 10f good-ground trip and now steps to 1m3f — if Gavin Ryan gets a clean passage from midfield in what will be a bunched, slow-tempo race, the horse's consistency makes it a serious threat to improve.

Connecteo is racing entirely out of its natural hold-up role and if it sets a genuinely slow pace up front unchallenged, it may lead longer than expected — Ben Coen is capable of producing a surprise front-running performance if allowed to bowl along undisturbed.

With 19 runners and virtually every horse a hold-up type, traffic and positional squeeze in the straight are a major factor — horses drawn wide or settled furthest back face a near-impossible task in a moderate-pace 1m3f race and should be viewed with caution regardless of ability.

Cadreville is worth monitoring each-way: the only horse in this field with a recent 3rd-place finish at 10f on good ground, a 7lb claimer in the saddle, and connections pointing at this longer trip — small field-sector discount but could outrun a wide price.

runners_data.name: Suzie Songs
runners_data.note: Won twice over six furlongs on good before finishing seventh over this course and distance last time; the lone confirmed front-runner here, her chance hinges entirely on how much company she gets for the lead — her STYLE_FIT flag is a consequence of that crowded-prominent field rather than any dramatic change in role, but she remains vulnerable if the pace gets contested.
runners_data.comment: Failed to settle down the field in a Group 3 at Leopardstown last time, a disappointing return that raises a slight question mark, but a pair of wins earlier in that sequence showed she's clearly up to this level. Course, distance and good ground are all proven, a first-time tongue-tie is added to help her relax, and with the trainer in good form, she's a leading danger on 91 despite that below-par latest run.

runners_data.name: Yaupon De Replay
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's yard is flying at 13/63 over the past 14 days, and this hold-up type represents the most natural beneficiary of a genuinely run race; his form over seven furlongs on soft was a respectable fourth and he has a course win on good, though his sample size of only three career runs demands some caution.
runners_data.comment: Down the field in a Group 3 at Chantilly last time, well below the level shown when winning two starts back, and this stable has a good record in this event, having taken it last year. Course and distance form is there, but 81 days since her latest outing and only a moderate recent level leave her the outsider of this six on a rating of 86.

runners_data.name: Frescobaldi
runners_data.note: A prominent racer with a win over seven furlongs on good, this course-and-distance form makes him the most straightforward fit for the expected race shape; Shane Foley rides and the horse has placed twice in seven outings at the trip, though his consistency record (153-50 recent form) hints at questions about holding form at a crucial moment.
runners_data.comment: Below-par down the field in a Listed race at Newbury last time, tried in cheekpieces without success, but that followed a good run of form beforehand, and a drop back in grade today should suit. Course, distance and good ground are all proven, and he's rated a leading danger on 89.

runners_data.name: Ocean's Breath
runners_data.note: Won over seven furlongs on good last time out and is a natural prominent type, but the overcrowded front-running section of this field means he is likely to either fight for position early or be bumped back against his nature — his chance is genuine on ability yet his race-position compromise is a real tactical risk to factor in.
runners_data.comment: Stepped up in trip to win a 3yo race at Fairyhouse by 3 lengths last time, backing up a progressive profile that suggests there's more to come back in handicap company. Course, distance and good ground are all proven, a first-time tongue-tie is added, and with the yard in excellent recent form, he heads our figures at 91 as the horse to beat.

runners_data.name: L L Koulsty
runners_data.note: Rory Mulligan takes the ride on this lightly-weighted 5lbs claimer; a winner twice in recent form, his best going is soft to heavy and he has no established form on good ground (0/0 placed from 1 run on similar going), making the conditions here a notable concern before the positional redistribution issue even comes into play.
runners_data.comment: A drop in trip suited when landing a handicap at Cork by 1 1/2 lengths last time, continuing a steady upward curve through his last five starts. Course, distance and good ground are all proven, and he's rated a leading danger on 90.

runners_data.name: Sir Benji
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's three-year-old won a ten-furlong maiden on heavy ground at the Curragh and has only two career runs — both at a mile and a quarter — so stepping back to seven furlongs on good turf at a higher level is a significant class-and-trip jump into the unknown; jockey Robert Whearty must help him adapt quickly to a shorter, sharper test.
runners_data.comment: Backed up a winning debut by matching that level when third in an auction race at Roscommon last time, and he's clearly held in high regard as a smart prospect. Today's step down in trip is the obvious question given he looks better served by galloping on further, with 10f his proven trip on easy or good going, leaving him respected but with a slight query on 88.

races.paceDynamic: Suzie Songs is the lone confirmed front-runner in a field of six and should stride to the front unchallenged from the off, setting a genuine but sustainable gallop over seven furlongs on good ground at Naas. The significant complication is that Ocean's Breath, L L Koulsty, and Sir Benji are all natural prominent racers who cannot all occupy their preferred early position — one or two will be forced to either fight for the spot and push the pace, or drop back against their nature and race in unfamiliar midfield territory. Suzie Songs therefore faces the real possibility of company at the front from Ocean's Breath or another crowding prominent type, which could transform a steady lead scenario into a contested, pressured gallop. This race shape most favours a horse capable of tracking the pace closely in second or third and quickening late from a genuine gallop — a true prominent-to-winner profile or a strong hold-up horse with a strong finishing kick, provided the pace holds honest.

watchPoints.text: Ocean's Breath and Suzie Songs — watch the first furlong closely; if Ocean's Breath breaks well from his gate and pushes forward, the resulting pace contest could fundamentally reshape the race and drain the leaders entering the straight.

Sir Benji — coming back from ten furlongs to seven furlongs for the first time represents a major unknown, and if he fails to settle on the sharp Naas track early it could compromise his run entirely.

L L Koulsty — no recorded form on good ground in five career starts, and all wins have come on soft or heavy; if the turf rides as described (good throughout) this is a serious profile concern that the market may not fully price.

Yaupon De Replay — watched for a clean run through the field; only three career starts means his hold-up style has had limited opportunity to be tested in truly competitive races, and a congested midfield traffic moment could end his chance prematurely.
